page: Microsoft Azure E4a_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 7452 processor. The instance provides 4 vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores with multithreading enabled, clocked at 3.35 GHz on an x86_64 architecture. It includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 16 MB of L3 cache. Memory capacity is configured at 32.0 GB RAM, establishing an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio typical of memory-heavy instance classes. Accelerated computing is absent, as the server carries no GPUs. Local ephemeral storage is bundled as a 107 GB SSD.

Benchmark outcomes demonstrate modest computational throughput, characterized by a Geekbench single-core score of 1346.0 and a multi-core score of 3095.0. Stress-ng scores show 757.99 for single-core and 1514.87 for multi-core processing, reflecting the lower-tier processing limits of its 2 physical AMD cores. Memory subsystem benchmarks show a read-only large-block throughput of 27.34 GB/sec and a write throughput of 12.95 GB/sec. Cryptographic performance on PassMark reached 4268.71, aided by hardware-accelerated AES and SHA extensions, while compression workloads scored 24.6 GB/sec in gzip.

The primary operational tradeoff of the E4a_v4 is its high memory allocation balanced against entry-level compute throughput. It suits caching layers, intermediate memory-bound databases, and internal web services that require a 1:8 core-to-memory footprint without requiring extensive compute-heavy operations. The instance does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses, which may necessitate additional routing configurations for external facing roles.
description: Microsoft Azure E4a_v4 is a memory-optimized instance featuring 4 vCPUs mapped across 2 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 7452 processor clocked at 3.35 GHz. Built on x86_64 architecture, the instance incorporates 32.0 GB of RAM, offering an expansive 8.0 GB memory-to-vCPU ratio. It features 107 GB of bundled local SSD storage and operates without dedicated GPU hardware. CPU benchmark evaluations reflect mid-tier single-core metrics alongside lower multi-core performance, such as a Geekbench multi-core score of 3095.0 and PassMark score of 5635.59. Supported instruction sets include AVX, AES, and SHA-NI, which maintain solid encryption capabilities. The instance delivers adequate memory density for memory-sensitive configurations, making it suited for caching nodes, small-to-midsize databases, Redis deployments, and intermediate enterprise applications requiring large memory buffers without dense computing requirements.
